For over a century, it had faithfully guided ships through thick fog and stormy seas.  Old Man Hemlock, the lighthouse keeper for the past 30 years, knew every creak and groan of the structure. He’d seen countless sunrises and sunsets paint the sky, and witnessed ships both arriving safely and, sadly, meeting their unfortunate end against the rocks. \n\nRecently, the lighthouse had been scheduled for modernization.  New automated systems were planned, replacing the manual light and the keeper’s duties.  Many villagers felt a sense of loss.  They cherished Old Man Hemlock’s stories and his familiar presence.  They worried that the automated system wouldn't possess the same understanding of the sea's moods as he did.  \n\nOne particularly foggy night, a large freighter lost its way.  The automated system failed due to a power surge, leaving the ship dangerously close to the rocks.  Old Man Hemlock, despite being officially retired, raced to the light room and manually activated the lamp, his years of experience guiding the vessel to safety.  The incident highlighted the irreplaceable value of human intuition and experience, even in the age of technology.  While the modernization project will eventually proceed, the villagers now understand that some things are simply too important to be automated.",
